blurb: A Japanese keep checked against photos from four sides: five roofs, gables placed face by face, white tile joints, a 14.85 m stone base.
18,038 iron parts on four legs, from the caissons dug under the Seine to the 300 m top.
Two thousand years of walls: the Roman enclosure, the royal double wall, the ruin, and Viollet-le-Duc’s slate roofs.
Four centuries of a city palace, placed on the French land registry with its real streets and neighbours.
Piers in open sea, two towers, cables spun wire by wire, then the deck hung from the towers outwards.
